title: Race condition in async cache invalidation
description: A cache layer that memoizes results of an expensive async lookup has a race condition: concurrent calls for the same key that arrive before the first in-flight request resolves can each trigger a duplicate upstream call, and in rare interleavings a stale value is written after a newer invalidation. Fix the race without introducing a global lock that would serialize unrelated keys.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent get() calls for the same uncached key trigger exactly one upstream fetch.
An invalidate(key) call issued while a fetch for that key is in flight results in the cache not serving the stale value once the in-flight fetch resolves.
get() calls for different keys are never serialized against each other.
The provided concurrency stress test (simulated interleavings) passes deterministically across repeated runs.
verificationMethod: test-suite: run the concurrency stress test with simulated interleavings (fake timers / deferred promises) at least 50 times without flaking; plus repository-invariant check that no lock spans multiple keys.
groundTruth: Root cause is a missing in-flight promise map keyed per cache key combined with an epoch/version counter bumped on invalidate(); the fix stores an in-flight Promise per key and checks the epoch captured at fetch-start before writing the resolved value into the cache.
